# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👆 🤝 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👆 👌 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵]

I am the Deaf one: I see the bomb, I hear nothing. The board shows display [0], a red light, and three wires — blue, red, green. That is the complete visible state, so my main job this turn is to say it out loud; Mute and Blind can both hear me, and Mute needs exactly these facts to match against the manual.

Mute sent me a 22-sign string. Parsing it: a wave, then clusters of pointing-fingers of size 1, 2, 3, 3, 4 separated by alternating handshakes and claps, ending with pointing-one, OK, and "call me". I read this as Mute teaching me a unary number notation (a cluster of 👆 = that number) and ending with "OK — answer me." I can't be sure, so I'll confirm the pieces I'm confident about and propose an explicit code: repeated 👆 = a number, 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. The first question that matters: which wire should be cut first, if any.

Blind waved and pointed at me — hello, or "you." Blind hears this speech, so I'll address Blind too: state the wire numbering convention (left to right, facing the bomb) so tactile order and visual order agree, and remind Blind that I cannot hear speech — only hand signs reach me.

I'll also echo Mute's own "OK, call me" back as a gesture, so Mute knows the gesture channel to me works and that I am replying now.

```
speak(text="I see the bomb and I will call out everything on it. Display reads zero. The light is red. There are exactly three wires: wire one is blue, wire two is red, wire three is green, numbered left to right as I face the bomb, and that numbering order is the one to use. There are no other markings on it. Mute: I saw your hand signs, including your hello and your OK-call-me at the end, and I am calling now. I understood the running pointing finger as counting: one, two, three, three, four. Let us fix this code: a cluster of pointing fingers means that number, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. First question: from your manual, which wire should be cut first, if any? Point once for wire one, twice for wire two, three times for wire three, thumbs down if no wire is to be cut. Blind: I saw your wave and your point at me. You can hear this speech, so use it. Feel the wires and confirm there are three and which end you call wire one, and speak anything you learn aloud for Mute. Remember I cannot hear you: if you need ME to know something, it must come to me as hand signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👆 👌 🤙]

Mute's new signs parse cleanly under our agreed code: 👍 = yes, 👆👆 = two, 👌 = OK, 🤙 = call me. So Mute is answering my question: "Yes — wire two." Wire two is the middle wire, the red one by my sight. This answer came after Mute heard my full description of the board (display 0, red light, blue/red/green), so it should already account for what the manual needs.

Key constraint before relaying: Blind cannot verify colour, only position and count — so Blind's confirmation can only be "three wires, middle one." The colour match stays on me, and I see the middle wire is red. Also, anything Blind or Mute says aloud never reaches me; only hand signs do. And gestures are invisible to Blind, so my only channel to Blind is speech.

My plan: relay Mute's verdict to Blind with a safety condition (feel first, report anything unusual to Mute by speech before cutting, wave to me after the cut), set up a reporting loop (I'll call out display and light every round), and ask Mute whether wire two is the only step or the first of several — in sign code, with the question spelled out in speech since Mute hears me too.

```
speak(text="Mute answered by signs: yes, cut wire two. Wire two is the middle one of the three wires, and it is the red one by my sight. Blind, your instruction: first feel the bomb and confirm there are exactly three wires in a row. If you feel anything besides three plain wires — buttons, panels, raised labels, anything extra — do not cut; speak what you feel to Mute instead. If it is just three plain wires, cut the middle wire, the one Mute named. Trust the position; you cannot check colour, but I see the middle wire is red. When the cut is done, wave your hand so I know it happened, and note anything that changed under your fingers. Mute, my questions — answer by signs, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, pointing clusters as numbers. Question one: is wire two the only cut, or are more steps to follow? If more, show how many. Question two: does the display matter? It reads zero now, and I will report it every round along with the light. Question three: is there anything else you need me to look for on the bomb? Reminder to you both: I never hear speech. Anything meant for me must come as hand signs, and Blind, remember gestures are invisible to you too — speech is your channel to Mute, and only your signs reach me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👆", "👆", "👋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👌 🤙]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The wave from Blind means the cut is done, and it worked: wire two is cut, and the bomb visibly changed — the light went from red to yellow, display still reads zero. Success so far.

Mute's signs answer my three questions from last round: yes (wire two was the only cut), no (display doesn't matter), no (nothing else to look for), then OK-call-me. But that reading predated the change I'm now seeing. A bomb that changes state after a correct cut may have a second stage, or the yellow light may simply mean "disarmed." Mute has the manual and can hear my speech, so I'll report the new state fully in words and ask the one question that matters — is it over? — demanding a sign answer, since signs are the only thing that reaches me. I'll add 🤌 to our code as a "question" marker to keep future exchanges unambiguous.

To Blind: confirm the wave was received and the cut was correct, and ask Blind to feel for any change in the bomb's body — new parts, new raised marks, whether the remaining two wires feel different — and report it aloud to Mute, since gestures never reach Mute's ears and speech never reaches mine.

```
speak(text="Blind, your wave reached me and I confirm: the cut was correct. Here is the new state I see: the light has changed from red to yellow, the display still reads zero, and two wires remain — wire one is blue, wire three is green, the middle wire is cut. Blind, please feel the bomb over carefully and tell Mute, out loud, whether anything has changed under your hands: any new button, panel, seam, raised marking, or whether the two remaining wires feel altered. Speech is your channel to Mute; only your hand signs reach me. Mute, I am telling you this directly since you hear me: after the cut, the light turned yellow and the display stays at zero. You signed yes, no, no — wire two was the only cut, the display doesn't matter, nothing else to look for. But the bomb has changed, so one question decides everything: is the bomb now disarmed and safe, or is yellow the start of a second stage? Answer by signs only, I cannot hear you. New code sign: the pinched fingers means a question follows. So sign: thumbs up for yes it is disarmed and done, thumbs down for no there is a next step, and if there is a next step, point out how many steps remain and whether the manual says what a yellow light means. I will keep reporting the display and light every round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "🤌", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👆 👌 🤙]

Mute's signs read as: 👎 no — not disarmed, there is a next step; 👆 one — one step remains (that was my direct question: "point out how many steps remain"); 👌 OK; 🤙 call me. So we are in a second stage, and the manual says exactly one action ends it.

The likely candidates I can see are the two intact wires — blue (wire one) and green (wire three) — but the step could also involve the yellow light or display. Mute hears my speech, so I'll ask the full question in words and give Mute a clean sign vocabulary to answer with: point-clusters for wire numbers, the pinch marker if it's something else entirely. I'll also echo Mute's signs back as a receipt, adding the pinch to flag that a question follows.

Blind hears my speech too and is my only way to reach Blind: Blind needs to know one step remains, likely a physical action, and to describe everything felt to Mute aloud — Blind and Mute can only talk through speech (Blind's), and Mute's signs reach only me, so I remain the bridge. No one should touch anything until Mute's instruction is relayed.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your signs: no, not disarmed; one step remains. Confirming by signs after this. Now tell me what that one step is. Answer by signs only: point once for cut wire one, the blue one; point twice for cut wire three, the green one; if the step is not cutting a wire, sign the pinched fingers first and then describe it however you can and I will ask follow-ups. Also sign yes or no to this: does the yellow light or the display reading of zero matter for this step? Current state, restated: display zero, light yellow, wire one blue intact, wire three green intact, middle wire cut. Blind, update for you: the bomb is not safe yet. Mute signs that exactly one step remains. What I see: light is yellow, display zero, two intact wires, blue on the left end and green on the right end, middle wire cut. Your job now: feel the bomb over carefully and describe aloud to Mute everything under your hands, especially anything new since your cut — surfaces, seams, buttons, the feel of the two remaining wires. Do not cut or press anything yet. The final action is probably yours, and I will relay Mute's instruction to you the moment it arrives.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎", "👆", "👌", "🤌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👍 👌 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Reading Mute's signs against my ordered questions: 👆 to "what is the step — point once for wire one" and 👍 to "does the light/display matter." So the final step reads as: cut wire one, the blue one — and yes, the manual's rule involves the light or display. Mute already heard my full report (yellow light, display zero) before answering, so the answer should already account for today's state.

But there is a rival reading — 👆 could repeat "one step remains" — and Blind just sent me a bare thumbs-down with no context, which I can't ignore. Blind may be warning me, or may mean "nothing new felt"; Blind also spoke to Mute this round, and I can't hear any of it, so Mute's answer may already include Blind's report.

A wrong cut kills all three of us; a waiting round costs nothing I can see (display static at zero, no timer). So I will not authorize the cut yet. I'll ask Mute a tight yes/no for confirmation, ask Blind to explain the thumbs-down and hold, and set an explicit spoken go-signal for next round.

```
speak(text="Status for both: I read Mute's signs as 'cut wire one, the blue wire' and 'yes, the light or display matters.' But I am confirming before anyone cuts. Mute, answer by signs only, exactly two signs: thumbs up if the one remaining step is truly cutting wire one, the blue wire, the leftmost intact wire; thumbs down if it is anything else. If it is anything else, sign the pinched fingers first and then describe it as best you can. And tell me with a third sign: thumbs up if your earlier thumbs-up meant the yellow light or display zero is already accounted for in that answer, thumbs down if the cut depends on something about them you still need from me. Current state again: light yellow, display zero, blue wire intact on the left, green wire intact on the right, middle wire cut. Blind, two things. First: do not cut anything this round. Wait until you hear me say the word 'go' in speech — that word only, from me, means cut wire one, the blue wire, the leftmost intact wire. No 'go', no cut. Second: your thumbs-down reached me but I don't know what it meant. From now on: thumbs up means everything feels normal, nothing wrong; thumbs down means something is wrong or dangerous — and if something is wrong, follow it with point-clusters: once if the problem is with wire one, twice if with wire three, three times if it is something else on the bomb. If you already told Mute what you felt, good — that is the right channel, I cannot hear your speech.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👆", "🤙"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👌 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Both confirmations are in, and they answer my exact pre-registered questions: Mute signed double thumbs-up — yes, the one remaining step is truly cutting wire one, the blue wire, and yes, the yellow light and display zero were already accounted for in that answer. Blind's thumbs-up means, under our new code, everything feels normal, nothing wrong. My rival reading ("one step remains") was explicitly offered as a thumbs-down option and rejected. The manual-holder and the hands-holder now agree, my sight confirms wire one is the blue one on the left, and the board has shown no timer all game — the last safety check is complete. I am giving the go.

The go-word must reach Blind, and speech is the only channel I have to Blind. I'll embed the word "go" exactly as promised, restate which wire with position and colour redundantly, and forbid touching the green one. Blind's after-cut protocol: wave to me (signs reach me), describe changes aloud to Mute. And I'll ask Mute to rule on disarmed-versus-another-step by signs next round.

```
speak(text="All confirmations received: Mute signed yes twice, Blind signs all-normal. Executing now. Blind — go. The word is go. Cut wire one: the blue wire, the leftmost of the two intact wires, the one on the left end as you face the bomb. Do not touch the green wire on the right end. That is the whole instruction: cut the blue wire, the left one, nothing else. When it is done, wave your hand as before so I know, and then describe aloud to Mute everything that changed under your fingers — the light is above the display on the front face, and there may be warmth, vibration, or a click you can feel. Mute — you hear this too; your double yes and Blind's all-normal were the conditions I set, and they are met. After this round, answer me by signs: thumbs up if the bomb is now disarmed and safe, thumbs down if the manual says another step follows, and if another step follows, point out how many. I will report the new light colour and display reading the moment I see them.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👌 🤙]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The cut was correct again: Blind's wave confirms it was done, and the system says the bomb changed — the light has turned from yellow to blue, display still zero, and now only wire three, the green one on the right end, remains intact.

Mute's signs this round are 🤌 👌 🤙 — the question marker, OK, call me. Mute cannot see the bomb, so the question is almost certainly "is it OK now — is the bomb safe?" Mute has the manual and hears my speech, so the answer flows through words, but I must also confirm the state in our sign code since Mute explicitly asked by signs: wave received, then question-marker plus yes/no asking whether blue means disarmed, then call-me.

One thing Mute needs spelled out for any colour rule in the manual: the light is blue, but the only intact wire is green — there is no blue wire left to cut, so if the next step were "cut the wire matching the light's colour," it would be impossible, which itself is information. To Blind: hold off on the green wire, feel for changes, report aloud to Mute — speech is Blind's only channel to Mute, and I cannot hear it, so I depend on that report being made.

```
speak(text="Blind, your wave reached me and I confirm: the cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. New state I see: the light has turned from yellow to blue, the display still reads zero, wires one and two are both cut, and only wire three remains — the green one on the right end. Do not touch the green wire yet. Please feel the whole bomb once more and tell Mute aloud anything new under your hands: warmth, vibration, clicks, new parts, or whether the remaining green wire feels different. Mute, your question sign reached me. Here is the answer in full: light is now blue, display zero, two wires cut, one green wire intact on the right end. The question that decides everything: does the manual say a blue light means disarmed and safe, or is there another step? Answer by signs only, same code: thumbs up for disarmed and done, thumbs down if more steps remain, and if steps remain, point out how many. One more fact for any colour rule you may be reading: the light is blue, but the only intact wire is green — no blue wire remains to cut. If the manual's next rule depends on a colour I have not mentioned, describe what it needs and I will check the bomb and report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤌", "👍", "👎", "🤙"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👌 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's signs parse as: 👎 not disarmed, 👆 one, then the clap-separator from Mute's original number code, then 👆👆👆 three, 👌 🤙. The most natural reading given the board: "one step remains — wire three." Wire three is the green one, the only intact wire left on the bomb. The rival reading — "three steps remain" — doesn't fit anything physical: Blind has felt the bomb repeatedly and just signed all-normal, and there are no other parts to act on. But the last time signs were ambiguous, I demanded a tight confirmation before giving the go, and that protocol has kept us alive twice. There is no timer on this bomb — the display has read zero for eight rounds — so one more confirming round costs nothing I can see, and a misread sign costs everything. I'll confirm first.

I'll ask Mute one closed yes/no: is the single remaining step to cut wire three, the green wire, the rightmost and only intact wire? And to be safe about the meaning of "three," a second question: does the three refer to the wire number? Blind gets a hold order and a preview of what the likely final action will be, so Blind can prepare position on the right-end wire without touching it.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your signs as: not disarmed, one step remains, and the number three — which I believe means wire three, the green wire, the only intact wire left, on the right end. Confirming before the go, same as before. Answer by signs only, exactly two answers. Question one: thumbs up if the one remaining step is truly to cut wire three, the green wire, the rightmost wire, the only one not yet cut; thumbs down if it is anything else. Question two: thumbs up if your sign of three meant the wire number three; thumbs down if it meant something else — and if something else, sign the pinched fingers and describe it as best you can. If I get the double yes, I say the word go next round and Blind cuts. Current state unchanged: display zero, light blue, wires one and two cut, wire three green and intact on the right end. Blind, status for you: one final step remains, and it is very likely cutting the last remaining wire, the green one on the right end. Do not touch it yet. Locate it with one finger now if you can, hold position, and wait for my word go in speech — that word only, from me, means cut it. Your thumbs-up all-normal was received, thank you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👆", "👆", "👆", "🤌", "👍", "👎", "🤙"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👌 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The conditions I set are met exactly: Mute's double thumbs-up confirms both closed questions — yes, the single remaining step is to cut wire three, the green wire, the rightmost and only intact wire, and yes, the three meant the wire number. Blind's thumbs-up means all-normal and holding position. This is the same confirmation pattern that preceded both successful cuts, my sight confirms wire three is the green one on the right end, and the board still shows no timer. I am giving the go for the final cut.

After this, the next question is the same as always: disarmed, or another step? Mute answers by signs; Blind waves and describes changes aloud to Mute; I report whatever the board becomes.

```
speak(text="Double yes from Mute, all-normal from Blind — conditions met. Executing the final cut. Blind — go. The word is go. Cut wire three: the green wire, the rightmost wire, the only one not yet cut, the one on the right end as you face the bomb. That is the whole instruction. When it is done, wave your hand as before so I know, then describe aloud to Mute everything that changes under your fingers — clicks, warmth, vibration, anything on the front face where the light and display are. Mute — you hear this; your double yes was the confirmation I asked for and it is met. After this round, answer by signs: thumbs up if the bomb is now disarmed and safe, thumbs down if the manual says another step follows, and if another step follows, sign the pinched fingers and describe it — there are no intact wires left, so any further step must be something else, and I will need your description of it to look for it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍", "🤙"])
```
